scope: Single guarded lane-B startup-only diagnostic after two owned-CDP endpoint timeouts; no product acceptance.

development_artifact.runtime_equivalent_to_workflow_checkout: No diffs in src, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or wxt.config.ts between the artifact source and the checkout used by this diagnostic.

endpoint_observation.interpretation: The endpoint appeared within the existing 8-second deadline in this admitted run. This run does not support increasing the deadline and does not prove endpoint timing under high CPU pressure.

resource_observations.process_attribution: Owned Chromium Helper and Chromium processes were among the highest observed CPU consumers; macOS system daemons also contributed.

interpretation: Chromium connected to CDP at 5.602 seconds, then entered the diagnostic's guarded panel/setup interval. The host later crossed the CPU-pending thresholds and the watchdog stopped the owned process group when CPU confirmation expired. The startup diagnostic did not complete its interval; its resource final is invalid, so it cannot establish sustained readiness or product behavior. No product defect is demonstrated.

related_unverified_attempt.endpoint_result: owned_cdp_endpoint_timeout at 8052 ms; child remained alive, endpoint was absent, and no UI observations were made.
related_unverified_attempt.resource_result: RESOURCE_CPU_PENDING at cpuBusyFraction 1.0 and one-minute load 10.5 on 4 logical CPUs; guest resource final invalid with exitCode 3.

decision: Do not change the 8-second default or retry guest Data from this evidence. Keep resource refusal intact. Any future hosted comparison needs a fresh peer-reviewed hypothesis and guarded admission; this single diagnostic is not a product pass.
limitations: One startup-only run on one hosted runner; no controlled high-CPU timing comparison was completed.
The CPU process interval uses bracketed process snapshots and centisecond process CPU time; short-lived, reparented, or PID-reused processes cannot be assigned exact interval CPU time.
